title: Dimension lower bound on torus fixed points of a proper homogeneous space
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $H\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], not necessarily smooth, connected or normal. Let $X=G/H$ be the separated finite-type $F$-scheme representing the fppf sheaf quotient of right cosets [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], and assume that $X$ is proper over $F$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $S\subseteq G$ be a torus: a closed subgroup scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,F}^{r}$ for some integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Give $X$ the left $S$-action induced by multiplication on $G$. Write $d=\dim X$ for its Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There are at least $d+1$ distinct points $x\in X(F)$ fixed scheme-theoretically by $S$: for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and every $s\in S(A)$ one has $s\cdot x_A=x_A$. No finiteness assumption on the set of fixed points is imposed, and $S$ need not be a maximal torus. The case $G=H$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$, is included.

source.place: Corollary 20.12, printed p.411, following Proposition 20.11, printed pp.410--411; the projective orbit realization used there is Theorem 7.18.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer], choose a nonzero finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ and a line $L$ whose stabilizer is exactly $H$ on every $F$-algebra. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] the map $gH\mapsto gL$ identifies $X$ with the reduced orbit of $[L]$ in $\mathbf P(V)$; [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] says that this orbit is locally closed. Thus this is a $G$-equivariant immersion $i:X\to\mathbf P(V)$, not merely a bijection on points. Projective space is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Since $X$ is proper over $F$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes $i$ proper; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] then makes it a closed immersion. In particular $X$ is nonempty (it contains the coset of $1$) and is a closed $S$-stable subscheme of this projective representation.

source.place: Corollary 20.12, printed p.411; Theorem 7.18 and its proof, printed p.143; Proposition 7.17, printed p.143.

proof.text: We prove the projective estimate needed here by induction on $N=\dim_F V-1$, simultaneously for every nonzero $S$-representation $V$ of this dimension and every nonempty closed $S$-stable subscheme $Z\subseteq\mathbf P(V)$: $Z$ has at least $\dim Z+1$ distinct scheme-theoretically $S$-fixed $F$-points. Nonreduced $Z$ are allowed. By [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-dimension], $\dim Z$ is the degree of its nonzero Hilbert polynomial, hence a finite nonnegative integer. We will also use $\dim\mathbf P^m_F=m$: its degree-$a$ homogeneous monomials form a basis of size $\binom{a+m}{m}$, a polynomial in $a$ of degree $m$, so the same cited theorem gives the equality. For $N=0$, the single standard chart in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] is $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Its only nonempty closed subscheme is itself, since a field has only the ideals $0,F$. The projective action on a one-dimensional representation is trivial over every algebra, so its unique point proves the base case.

source.place: Proposition 20.11, printed pp.410--411; induction reformulated on the ambient projective dimension so that reducible and nonreduced hyperplane sections require no component-invariance lemma.

proof.text: Suppose $N\geq1$ and assume the induction assertion in ambient dimension $N-1$. Use [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to choose an $S$-eigenbasis $e_0,\ldots,e_N$ with characters $\chi_i$. Use the separating-cocharacter clause of [lem-sfb-projective-torus-fixed-weight-schemes] to choose $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to S$ such that different occurring characters have different integer weights $m_\chi$ under $\lambda$. Number the basis so $m_0$ is minimal. Put $W=\langle e_1,\ldots,e_N\rangle$ and $Q=\mathbf P(W)=\{z_0=0\}\subseteq\mathbf P(V)$. Both $W$ and $Q$ are $S$-stable. On the standard charts this hyperplane is obtained by imposing the equation $z_0/z_j=0$ for $j\ne0$, so it is a closed subscheme isomorphic to $\mathbf P^{N-1}_F$; these chart descriptions are those of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Let $Y=Z\times_{\mathbf P(V)}Q$, with its scheme-theoretic intersection structure. It is a closed $S$-stable subscheme of $\mathbf P(W)$.

source.place: Proposition 20.11, printed pp.410--411; Theorem 12.12, pp.234--235, and Lemma 13.51, p.274.

proof.text: If $|Z|\subseteq|Q|$, then $|Y|=|Z|$ with the same topology, hence $\dim Y=\dim Z$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Apply the induction hypothesis to $Y\subseteq\mathbf P(W)$; its $\dim Z+1$ fixed points give that many fixed points in $Z$ by the equivariant inclusion. This uses the intersection $Y$, not an unjustified factorization of a possibly nonreduced $Z$ through $Q$. Otherwise $U=Z\setminus|Q|$ is a nonempty open subset of the finite-type $F$-scheme $Z$. The density assertion of [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], applied to the closed subset $Z$ of itself, gives a closed point of $Z$ in $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] its residue field is $F$, so choose $z=[e_0+\sum_{i=1}^N a_i e_i]\in U(F)$.

source.place: Proposition 20.11, printed p.411, the hyperplane-containment case and the choice of a point outside it; nonreduced containment handled by the scheme-theoretic intersection.

proof.text: On the chart $D_+(z_0)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], define $\gamma:\mathbf A^1_F\to D_+(z_0)$ by the polynomial coordinates $z_i/z_0\mapsto a_i t^{m_i-m_0}$. All exponents are nonnegative. On $\mathbf G_m$ this is $\lambda(t)z$ by the eigenbasis formula of [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition], so it factors through $Z$ there. The pullback of every equation of $Z\cap D_+(z_0)$ is a polynomial zero in $F[t,t^{-1}]$, hence zero in $F[t]$ since localization of this domain is injective. Thus $\gamma$ factors through $Z$ on all of $\mathbf A^1$. Its value $p=\gamma(0)$ has $z_0=1$ and only coordinates of weight $m_0$ possibly nonzero. Separation of the weights says these coordinates all have character $\chi_0$. Consequently, for every $F$-algebra $A$ and $s\in S(A)$ the vector representing $p_A$ is multiplied by the unit $\chi_0(s)$. Its line is unchanged; the equivariant closed inclusion then gives $s p_A=p_A$ in $Z(A)$. Hence $p$ is scheme-theoretically fixed and lies outside $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 20.11, printed p.411, the nonnegative-weight affine-chart limit, expanded explicitly in polynomial coordinates.

proof.text: Write $d_Z=\dim Z$. If $d_Z=0$, the point $p$ already supplies the required $d_Z+1=1$ fixed point. If $d_Z\geq1$, step 2 gives $\dim Q=N-1$; apply [lem-sfb-projective-closed-intersection-dimension] to the two nonempty closed subsets $|Z|,|Q|$ of $\mathbf P^N_F$. Its hypothesis is $d_Z+(N-1)\geq N$, and its conclusion is that $Y$ is nonempty with $\dim Y\geq d_Z-1$. The induction hypothesis in ambient dimension $N-1$ supplies at least $\dim Y+1\geq d_Z$ distinct fixed $F$-points in $Y$. Adding $p\notin Y$ proves the induction step. This constructs only the required finite list, whether or not the entire fixed set is finite.

source.place: Proposition 20.11, printed p.411; its use of Lemma 20.10 is supplied by Stacks Tag 0B2R, varieties-lemma-intersection-in-projective-space.

proof.text: Apply the established induction assertion to the closed $S$-stable image $i(X)$ in step 1. A closed immersion identifies its source with its scheme-theoretic image and preserves the topology, so its dimension is $d$. The equivariant identification carries the $d+1$ distinct fixed $F$-points back to $X$, and the equalities after every algebra extension carry back with them. This gives exactly the stated scheme-theoretic fixedness. Nothing required maximality of $S$, smoothness of $H$, or finiteness of the fixed set. When $S$ is trivial all the character weights coincide, and the same coordinate construction is constant; when $G=H$ the estimate reduces to the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Corollary 20.12, printed p.411, final application of the projective estimate.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 20.12 and Proposition 20.11, printed pp.410--411; the same hyperplane/extra-fixed-point proof, with induction on ambient dimension, explicit polynomial limit, and the existing Stacks 0B2R intersection theorem.

Step 5: the polynomial limit gamma is a genuine morphism to Z because F[t] injects into F[t,1/t]; p = gamma(0) carries only character chi_0, so it is fixed after every algebra extension, and p is not in Y. Step 6: 0B2R is applied with r = d_Z, s = N-1, which is valid exactly when d_Z >= 1; d_Z = 0 is handled separately. Step 7 transports back to X. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and each step's bracket citations equal its uses. No SGA. Edge cases: r = 0, G = H, sharp G_m on P^n, nonreduced Z, infinite fixed locus.
